stories.delivered_paragraph: Paramount Skydance has asked a federal judge to begin its antitrust trial over the proposed Warner Bros. merger in November, while a 12-state coalition and the Writers Guild of America want an April 5, 2027 start. The states contend the $111 billion deal would reduce competition in basic cable and theatrical distribution, and Paramount will owe Warner shareholders $7 million a day from Sept. 30 until closing. The trial calendar could therefore materially affect both the merger’s cost and its completion timetable.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Fender Musical Instruments has demanded that makers of Stratocaster-style guitars, including companies contacted in Europe such as Yamaha and PRS, pull the models from the market after asserting newly acquired copyright protection for the design. Some manufacturers have agreed to redesign instruments, while others are challenging Fender through lawyers and litigation. The dispute will test whether a decades-old, widely copied guitar shape can be controlled through copyright—and could reshape the market for lower-cost compatible instruments.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Indian consumers spent a record $345 million on mobile apps in the second quarter, up 35% from a year earlier, as payments for generative AI, streaming and productivity services rose, Sensor Tower said. Revenue per download has more than doubled in three and a half years even as quarterly downloads have held near 6.3 billion since 2023. The shift gives app developers a more credible path to earning subscription revenue in the world’s biggest download market.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Amazon, Alphabet and Tesla each reported negative cash flow in their latest quarters, while Meta’s cash generation fell 91%, highlighting the financial strain of the technology industry’s AI buildout. The results come as companies race to fund data centers and computing equipment despite rising component costs. Investors are increasingly focused not just on AI revenue potential, but on whether the spending surge can be financed without weakening balance sheets or returns.

stories.delivered_paragraph: President Donald Trump said the Justice Department’s proposed “anti-weaponization” fund is dead but also said he wished it were not, reopening a dispute that has stalled acting Attorney General Todd Blanche’s confirmation. Republican Sens. John Cornyn and Thom Tillis have demanded written assurances that the fund will not proceed, and Tillis said Trump’s remarks suggested it remained alive. Their resistance leaves Blanche’s nomination dependent on resolving concerns over potential taxpayer-funded compensation.

stories.delivered_paragraph: MarketWatch warned that workers who delay claiming Social Security until age 70 should weigh more than the larger initial check: the higher benefit also receives proportionally larger cost-of-living adjustments. The point adds a household-level complication to the broader debate over the program’s funding shortfall. Claiming decisions can permanently alter retirement income, making the timing trade-off important even as policymakers focus on Social Security’s long-term finances.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Rescuers have recovered the body of U.S. climber Mallory Geis after an avalanche struck a 10-person expedition on Pakistan’s Broad Peak, and authorities also identified victims from Oman and Nepal. Geis, 39, was from San Antonio, according to U.S. media; bad weather has hampered the search, with one climber still unaccounted for. Drone teams have spotted several others, but rescuers must reach the high-altitude site before their condition can be confirmed.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Hamas said it will disarm only after Israel fulfills earlier ceasefire commitments, qualifying President Donald Trump’s claim of a breakthrough in U.S.-brokered Gaza negotiations. The group’s position leaves a central condition of any lasting agreement unresolved despite Trump’s announcement. Whether Israel meets the commitments Hamas cites—and whether Hamas ultimately accepts disarmament—will determine whether the reported diplomatic progress can move beyond a public claim into an enforceable deal.

stories.delivered_paragraph: An estimated 60,000 people from Morocco crossed into Spain’s North African enclave of Ceuta over 24 hours, an unprecedented influx into a territory with about 83,000 residents. Dozens died attempting the crossing, though Spanish officials said more than 48,000 migrants had voluntarily returned to Morocco by Friday evening. The surge has put renewed pressure on Spain and Morocco to explain what triggered it and to manage a border route long used by people seeking entry to Europe.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Sony and Marvel’s “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” took in a record $72 million in domestic previews and was tracking toward a $167 million to $173 million opening day, according to industry estimates. Forecasts for its North American debut ranged from roughly $270 million to above $330 million, putting it within reach of the biggest openings ever but still short of a confirmed record. Its performance will be a major test of whether superhero films can again deliver event-scale theatrical crowds.

stories.delivered_paragraph: The expansion Toronto Tempo acquired forward Aneesah Morrow from the Connecticut Sun for the rights to Maria “Masha” Kliundikova and a 2028 second-round pick. Morrow, the No. 7 pick in last year’s draft, averaged 11.6 points and 8.9 rebounds in 23.2 minutes over 20 games this season, including nine double-doubles. The deal gives Toronto the young frontcourt player it had been seeking while Connecticut adds future roster flexibility.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Atlanta’s ONE Musicfest has canceled its 2026 event after 16 years, saying it will use the pause to rethink and build a new version of the festival rather than repeat its established format. Last year’s lineup included Future, Mary J. Blige, Ludacris, Kehlani and Doechii, reflecting the festival’s mix of rap and R&B generations. The decision removes a significant annual gathering from Atlanta’s concert calendar while organizers work on a possible relaunch.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Microsoft, Amazon and Alphabet added nearly $1.5 trillion in combined market value this week after reporting strong cloud growth and affirming or increasing AI capital-spending plans. Microsoft gained more than $600 billion, while Amazon and Alphabet each rose by more than $400 billion; investors viewed the results as evidence that returns on AI investment may be emerging. The gains sharpened a divide among megacaps, with Meta and Apple losing value as investors questioned their spending outlooks.

stories.delivered_paragraph: The S&P 500 finished July lower, its first decline for the month since 2014, after a volatile final stretch of trading. Chip stocks led the pullback, posting their worst monthly performance in 24 years, according to MarketWatch. The reversal shows how quickly investor enthusiasm around technology can fade when concerns about valuations, spending and the durability of the AI-led rally begin to outweigh recent gains.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Index Ventures has raised $2 billion across three new funds, bringing its total available investing capital to $3.5 billion shortly after its payout from the Wiz cybersecurity deal. The fresh capital gives the venture firm substantial capacity to back startups across stages despite a selective market for technology investing. It also signals that established investors with recent exits can continue deploying money even as many younger companies face tougher fundraising conditions.
